disputed.question: Which $jsonSchema keywords do create and collMod accept on the managed service?
disputed.reason: The closing clause 'the engine-source dispatch list in DECISIONS topic 10 matches the managed service' generalises from a subset. Of the 23 dispatch-list keywords, only 7 were exercised as accepted: properties, required, bsonType, description, title, enum and oneOf. 'type' was tested only in its rejected 'integer' form. Not exercised: pattern (which DECISIONS tells filings to keep), multipleOf, minimum/maximum and their exclusive forms, minLength/maxLength, items, additionalItems, minItems/maxItems, uniqueItems, encrypt and encryptMetadata. Also untested: $ref, default, definitions and id (4 of the 6 'not supported at this time' keywords) and dot-notation property paths. In current engine source, title is also gated by a GUC (EnableBsonTypeArgumentValidation, bson_json_schema_tree.c lines 201-206), so how the dispatch list behaves depends on the service's build and GUC settings. Supported wording: every keyword tested behaved as the dispatch list predicts. The rest of this conclusion follows from the raw responses.

disputed.question: What does this mean for DECISIONS topic 10 open item 1 (engine build, enum/oneOf live, validator enablement path)?
disputed.reason: 'Filings can say validators work out of the box on current clusters' is a generalisation from one cluster (created the same day, eastus, M30, server 8.0, documentdb_versions 2.2-1/2.3.0/12.1-1), and the answer's own last sentence says older clusters, regions and server versions were not tested. DECISIONS topic 10 cites Microsoft Q&A 5891204 (2026-05-14), which reported 'validator not supported yet' on a server 8.0 M20 cluster, and a Q&A answer describing a service-side rollout. Engine source marks EnableSchemaValidation 'Added in v0.108, enabled in v0.114' (feature_flag_configs.c line 22). So existing clusters on older builds, other tiers (M10/M20/free) and other regions may still be gated. Also, 'the remaining unsupported keywords fail with 9 FailedToParse' is shown only for the 11 rejected keywords tested. Supported wording: on a cluster created 2026-11-25 in eastus (M30, 8.0), validators worked with no cluster-level previewFeatures, no subscription feature registration and no configuration change, and enum and oneOf are live there.

disputed.question: Extra (beyond the spec list): are title/description, $schema, format and type 'integer' accepted?
disputed.reason: The last sentence is not observed: no generated schema was tested. It says generated JSON Schemas (Pydantic, zod) must be stripped of $schema and format and must use bsonType int/long. That list is incomplete by this run's own evidence. anyOf and additionalProperties are also rejected here, and they are typical of generated schemas: Pydantic emits anyOf for Optional fields plus default values, and zod-to-json-schema emits $schema and additionalProperties: false by default. $ref, $defs and default were not tested. Also, 'title and description (top level and on a property)' overstates the test. The validator put title only at the top level; only description appeared on a property, while Pydantic puts title on every property. Supported wording: $schema, format and type 'integer' are rejected with code 9; title and description at the top level, and description on a property, are accepted and required is still enforced.

disputed.question: Do bypassDocumentValidation, validationAction 'warn' and collMod-attached validators behave as in MongoDB?
disputed.reason: For 'warn', the answer 'yes, as in MongoDB' rests on one accepted violating insert (A0warn.insert, n=1). v_warn's stored options were never read back, and no warning or log was observed. In MongoDB, warn accepts the write and logs the violation. Current engine source skips validation entirely when validationAction is 'warn': CheckSchemaValidationEnabled in schema_validation.h requires ValidationAction_Error, and schema_validation.c line 188 says 'If validationAction is warn, skip validation'. So 'as in MongoDB' holds only for the outcome the client sees, and advice to use warn to audit violations would not carry over. Supported wording: a violating insert is accepted under validationAction 'warn'. The bypass and collMod parts are supported by controlled comparisons (A0c vs A0d; A0cm.insert, A6.enum, A6.oneOf).

disputed.question: Where does the managed service differ from open-source 0.117 in this test?
disputed.reason: The answer lists hello.internal.documentdb_versions and kind 'azuredocumentdb' as differences, but the open-source 0.117 run never compared them. Its run_test.py (line 89) recorded only maxWireVersion, minWireVersion, maxWriteBatchSize and maxBsonObjectSize from hello. The current open-source gateway also appends internal: {documentdb_versions, kind} (ismaster.rs line 119), with kind taken from the setup field instance_kind (empty by default). So this is at most a difference in values, and it was not observed. Observed differences: maxWireVersion 25 vs 21, buildInfo.version 8.0.0 vs 7.0.0, and statsEnabled: true in the listCollections options. The rest of the answer (every code, codeName, errmsg, errInfo absence and createIndexes shape matched) is verified.

extra_observations: Secrets scan of all 11 files in m-schema: the password (raw and URL-encoded), the URIs, both host names, the cluster name and the 12-character admin user name appear nowhere. The only '@' characters are in regex patterns in run_test.py. The only GUID is the scratchpad session folder in file paths. The resource-group name appears 3 times; it is given in the task and is not a secret. No redaction was needed.

Every step's response in report.json matches the compact report in the task. With ObjectIds and ms timings normalised, report.rerun.json is identical to run 1 for all 92 scripted steps, covering raw responses and command texts as well as outcomes. run_stdout.txt and run_stdout.rerun.txt differ only in the output file name.

Read-only control-plane checks run by the reviewer; nothing on the cluster was changed. A fresh 'az documentdb mongocluster show' (extension documentdb 1.0.0, API 2026-06-01; previewFeatures is in its show schema) still shows no previewFeatures and lastModifiedAt equal to createdAt (2026-11-25T20:35:33.2901136Z), matching M3 and the orchestrator's earlier show.raw.json. 'az feature list --namespace Microsoft.DocumentDB' shows all 232 features NotRegistered, and the tenant is not Microsoft's corporate tenant. No cluster-level or subscription-level preview flag explains why validators are on; service-side flighting cannot be ruled out from the client.

M3's recorded command is a paraphrase (a <cluster> placeholder and a pseudo '| select' pipe). Neither the selection script nor any raw output was saved. finalize.py also marks M3 rerun_consistent: true, although M3 was never rerun (report.rerun.json has 92 steps without it). The reviewer's fresh read agrees with M3.

Open-source comparison verified against engine-tests/jsonschema-and-partial-unique/report.json. Of the 51 managed steps with an open-source counterpart, all match on code, codeName, errmsg, errInfo presence, counts and index specs except A0b (extra statsEnabled: true). M1 and M2 differ in wire version and buildInfo version. Every topic-10 bullet in ENGINE-TESTS.md also holds on the managed cluster. The open-source run used insertOne/insertMany, whose WriteError does not carry top-level errorLabels, so 'no errorLabels on writes' could only be checked on the managed run (raw commands).

Several conclusions are labelled vs_open_source 'same' while covering sub-claims never run on open-source: the C.* query-operator steps, additionalProperties_with_id, enforcement after collMod, update, findAndModify, warn, the non-unique $exists:false index and the unique+sparse control. Most answers say so, but the answer for the unique+sparse conclusion does not.

Engine-source citations check out. error_mappings.csv line 45 reads '121,DocumentFailedValidation' at commit a5f16362, committed 2026-11-18. MongoDB's name for code 121 is DocumentValidationFailure. Current engine main defaults EnableSchemaValidation to true ('enabled in v0.114') and gates title on EnableBsonTypeArgumentValidation ('Added in v1.2'), so title acceptance may differ on open-source 0.117; it was not tested there.

Observed in B1c, B1g, B2c, B2i and B4d, and the same on open-source: duplicate-key write errors carry only {index, code: 11000, errmsg: 'Duplicate key violation on the requested collection: Index <name>'}. There is no 'E11000 duplicate key error' prefix and no keyPattern or keyValue, so code that parses the MongoDB message or reads keyValue will not work.

Not exercised on the managed service, beyond what the tester lists (validationLevel 'moderate', $merge/$out, other clusters, regions and server versions, the global host): pattern, numeric, string and array validators, the 'type' keyword with a valid JSON type, $ref/default/definitions/id, $defs, and dot-notation property paths.
summary: The test is sound. Every response in report.json matches the compact report. The rerun reproduces all 92 scripted steps exactly once ObjectIds and timings are normalised, covering raw responses and commands as well as outcomes. The open-source comparison is correct: the 51 counterpart steps match except the extra statsEnabled in A0b, and only metadata differs otherwise (wire version 25 vs 21, buildInfo 8.0.0 vs 7.0.0). No password, e-mail address or identifier is in the test folder. These observed facts hold: collection validators are on with no cluster-level previewFeatures and no subscription feature registration (re-checked read-only by the reviewer); enum, oneOf, title and description are accepted, and enum and oneOf are enforced, including after collMod and in find; additionalProperties, allOf, anyOf, not, patternProperties, dependencies, minProperties, maxProperties, $schema, format and type 'integer' fail with code 9 FailedToParse; violating insert and update return write error 121 with no codeName, errInfo or errorLabels; violating findAndModify returns ok:0, 121, codeName DocumentFailedValidation, as in the open-source error_mappings.csv; partial unique indexes, the $exists:false rejection (67) and the sparse-mix rejection (197) behave as on open-source 0.117. Five conclusions need narrower wording. (1) 'The dispatch list matches the managed service' rests on 7 of 23 dispatch-list keywords. (2) 'Validators work out of the box on current clusters' generalises from one new eastus M30 8.0 cluster, against a May 2026 report of 'validator not supported yet' on an 8.0 M20 cluster. (3) The Pydantic/zod guidance was not tested and leaves out anyOf and additionalProperties, which this run shows are rejected; title was tested only at the top level. (4) 'warn behaves as in MongoDB' rests on one accepted insert, and engine source skips validation in warn mode rather than logging it. (5) hello.internal was never captured on open-source, so it cannot be listed as a difference.
